# Set up your account and sign in safely

An editor account can publish to the public site, so it is worth protecting well. This guide covers your own
account: your name and password, two extra ways to keep it safe, and a few choices that make the Control Plane suit you.

After reading this guide, you will know:

- How to open your account.
- How to change your password.
- How to turn on two-factor sign-in, and what to do with the recovery codes.
- How to add a passkey.
- How to change the theme, your start page and what happens after you save.
- What to do if you forget your password.

## 1. Open your account

The circle with your initials, top right, opens a menu. Choose **Manage profile**.

The buttons at the top are **Passkeys**, **Two-Factor Authentication** and **Change Password**. Below them are your
name and email address, then **Preferences**.

To change your name, edit it and choose **Save**. Your email address is shown but can't be changed here. Ask an
administrator.

## 2. Change your password

1. Choose **Change Password**.
2. Enter your current password, then the new one twice.
3. Choose **Change Password** again.

> [!NOTE]
> Changing your password signs you out everywhere else. That is useful if you think someone else knows it.

## 3. Turn on two-factor sign-in

With two-factor sign-in, a stolen password is not enough. Each time you sign in you also enter a six-digit code from an
authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password.

1. Choose **Two-Factor Authentication**, then **Enable two-factor authentication**.
2. In your authenticator app, scan the QR code. If you can't scan it, type the **Setup key** instead.
3. Enter the six-digit code the app shows, in **Verification code**, and choose **Confirm**.
4. Nibble shows your **Recovery codes**. Copy them and keep them somewhere safe, such as a password manager.
   Choose **I've saved them**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Recovery codes are shown only once. Each one signs you in one time if you lose your phone. Without them, you will
> need an administrator's help to get back in.

Your account page's menu then shows how many recovery codes are left. Choose **New recovery codes** for a fresh set
(your password is asked for). The old codes stop working.

**Turn off** switches the authenticator app off. Your role may require it, in which case the button isn't offered
unless you have a passkey.

## 4. Add a passkey

A passkey lets you sign in with your device's fingerprint, face or screen lock instead of a password.

1. Choose **Passkeys**, then **Add passkey**.
2. Name it so you know which device it is, for example "Work laptop".
3. Choose **Continue** and follow your browser's prompt.

The list shows when each passkey was added and last used. **Rename** gives one a new name. **Remove** stops that device
signing you in. If the button isn't there, your browser doesn't support passkeys.

## 5. Choose how the Control Plane works for you

Under **Preferences**:

| Choice | Does |
|---|---|
| **Theme** | **System** follows your device. **Light** and **Dark** stay as they are. |
| **Start page** | where you land after signing in: the **Dashboard**, or one of your collections |
| **After saving** | **Keep editing** stays on the page. **Go to the list** returns to the listing. **Create another** opens a new blank entry. |

These save as you change them, and apply to you only.

## 6. If you forget your password

On the sign-in page, choose **Forgot password?**, enter your email address and follow the email. If no
email arrives, ask an administrator to send you a password reset.

## 7. When you are signed out

After a while without activity Nibble signs you out. A warning comes first, with an **Extend Session** button, so what
you are writing is not lost. If something goes wrong anyway, see
[Save, preview and publish](publishing.md#8-if-a-save-goes-wrong).
